original_question: For fixed r >= 1 and m edges, which B_{2,r+1}-free non-bipartite graph has the largest spectral radius?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 6, sharpened immediately by Conjecture 3.8: the non-bipartite edge-spectral problem for forbidden book graphs B_{2,r+1}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical object and optimization task: r is fixed, the graph has m edges, the forbidden subgraph is B_{2,r+1}, the graph is required to be non-bipartite, and the goal is to identify the graph with maximum adjacency spectral radius. That is exactly the content of Problem 6 in Section 3. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
missing_details: The paper works with finite, simple, undirected graphs; in the general edge-spectral setup it also introduces 𝒢(m,F) as the class of F-free graphs with m edges and no isolated vertices. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.19395v1))

B_{2,r+1} should be defined explicitly as the book graph K_2 ∨ (r+1)K_1, equivalently the graph obtained from K_{2,r+1} by adding an edge between the two vertices of degree r+1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
The paper's sharper formulation is asymptotic: it is not for arbitrary m, but for m sufficiently large (with r fixed). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
The spectral quantity should be named explicitly as λ(G), the adjacency spectral radius. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.19395v1))

The paper does not leave the optimum informal; Conjecture 3.8 introduces an explicit extremal value ρ(m,r), defined as the largest root of x^3 - x^2 - (m-1)x + m - 2r - 1 = 0. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
The conjectured equality case is conditional: equality is expected only when m ≡ 1 (mod r). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
The extremal graph candidate should be stated explicitly as K^+_{r,(m-1)/r}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
The notation K^+_{a,b} must be defined: it is obtained from K_{a,b} by adding one edge inside the part of size b. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, polynomial-degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; this is purely a graph-spectral extremal problem.
refined_question: For each fixed integer r ≥ 1, does there exist m_0(r) such that, for every m ≥ m_0(r), every finite simple non-bipartite B_{2,r+1}-free graph G with m edges satisfies λ(G) ≤ ρ(m,r), where B_{2,r+1} = K_2 ∨ (r+1)K_1, ρ(m,r) is the largest root of x^3 - x^2 - (m-1)x + m - 2r - 1 = 0, and equality holds if and only if m ≡ 1 (mod r) and G is isomorphic to K^+_{r,(m-1)/r}, with K^+_{a,b} obtained from K_{a,b} by adding an edge inside the part of size b? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
justification: The draft is aiming at the book-graph part of Section 3, not the introduction. Problem 6 is the nearest official open problem matching your wording almost verbatim: it asks for the extremal graph with maximum spectral radius among all B_{2,r+1}-free non-bipartite graphs with m edges. Immediately after that, the authors state Conjecture 3.8, which is their more precise intended formulation of the same problem: it gives the asymptotic quantifier ('m sufficiently large'), the exact spectral upper bound via ρ(m,r), and the proposed equality case K^+_{r,(m-1)/r}. The surrounding context also supplies the notation B_{2,r+1} = K_2 ∨ (r+1)K_1, the definition of K^+_{a,b}, and the general meaning of λ(G) and 𝒢(m,F). Therefore the refined question above stays as close as possible to the paper's actual intent while making all hidden assumptions explicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))
